title: DPYD c.557A>G (rs115232898) decreased-function allele

a_function.statement: CPIC classifies DPYD c.557A>G as Decreased function, activity value 0.5, with the diplotype phenotypes applied here.
a_function.independence: NOT independent: both are CPIC products. Recorded per the definitional-claim rule.
a_function.independent_support: PMID:24648345 (functional, independent of CPIC); its ~15% Y186C reduction is recorded as a limitation of the effect size, not of the classification.

b_coordinates.statement: GRCh37 plus strand 1:98165030, ref T (normal), alt C (carrier).
sources: VariantValidator on coding HGVS without an rsID
b_coordinates.independence: Ensembl and VariantValidator agree; VariantValidator was queried on coding HGVS so it is not the same dbSNP record.

c_ancestry.statement: The allele occurs predominantly in people of African ancestry.
c_ancestry.independence: Independent: gnomAD is a population-sequencing dataset with no cohort, dataset or upstream assertion shared with Cunha-Junior's 115 African Brazilians. gnomAD v2.1.1 exomes give African allele frequency 0.0230 vs non-Finnish European 0.000053 (~435x), with 374 of 417 alt alleles in the African group; the genomes give African 0.0187 against 0.0 in the non-Finnish European, Latino/Admixed American, Ashkenazi Jewish, East Asian and Finnish groups, with the pooled 'Other' group at 0.00368 as the only other non-zero genome group.
c_ancestry.note: Offer 2014 (PMID:24648345) is retained only as context: it states that the deficient variants it newly classified are rare in Europeans and occur at appreciable frequencies in other populations, which is a statement about a GROUP of variants and does not by itself establish the distribution of c.557A>G. It is no longer counted toward the two-source rule for this claim (raised in review of #2452).
c_ancestry.correction: An earlier revision of this manifest and README stated the genomes were 0.0 in every other population. The committed payload shows the pooled 'Other' group at 0.00368, so that phrasing was false and is corrected. Caught in review of PR #2452; the African-predominance conclusion is unaffected.
c_ancestry.context_only_reason: Offer 2014 supports a statement about the GROUP of deficient variants it newly classified being rare in Europeans and at appreciable frequencies elsewhere; it is not allele-specific for c.557A>G. Kept for context and deliberately excluded from `sources` so no consumer counts it toward the two-source rule for this claim. Raised in review of PR #2452, which noted that leaving it in `sources` made the machine-readable mapping contradict the narrative.
c_ancestry.measure_comparability: The two sources are NOT directly comparable as published and must not be presented as numerically agreeing. Cunha-Junior report 3 heterozygotes among 115 people = 2.61% CARRIER PREVALENCE, which is 3 variant copies among 230 chromosomes = 1.30% ALLELE FREQUENCY. gnomAD's 2.30% is an allele frequency, implying ~4.50% carrier prevalence under Hardy-Weinberg. On a common denominator gnomAD's African allele frequency is about 1.76x Cunha-Junior's, which is unsurprising given different populations (gnomAD African/African-American vs admixed African Brazilians) and sample sizes (16,250 vs 230 chromosomes). What both establish independently is the African-predominant DISTRIBUTION, which is the only thing this packet claims. An earlier revision asserted the percentages agreed; that compared a carrier prevalence with an allele frequency and was corrected after review of PR #2452.
